changes.old: Creates a data center development and incentive program with a 100 percent state sales/use tax exemption for certified data centers, a 250 million dollar minimum investment threshold, job and labor commitments, utility consultation, water stewardship, backup power requirements, and targeted resource acquisition authority.
changes.new: Would create a data center development and incentive program with a 100 percent state sales/use tax exemption for certified data centers, a $250 million minimum investment threshold, job and labor commitments, utility consultation, water stewardship, backup power requirements, and targeted resource acquisition authority.

changes.old: Would authorize consumer-regulated electric utilities to serve new nonresidential loads, including data centers, outside ordinary public utility regulation unless they interconnect with a regulated utility service territory.
changes.new: As introduced, would exempt qualifying consumer-regulated electric generation and supply systems serving new nonresidential loads, including data centers, from public utility regulation unless they elect to interconnect with the grid in a regulated public utility service territory; public safety and environmental oversight would remain.

changes.old: Would have created the Colorado Data Center Development and Grid Modernization Act, including certification tiers, sales/use tax exemptions, grid enhancement credits, utility consultation, renewable/clean energy commitments, water stewardship, and annual compliance reports.
changes.new: As introduced, would create the Colorado Data Center Development and Grid Modernization Act, including certification tiers, sales/use tax exemptions, grid enhancement credits, utility consultation, renewable/clean energy commitments, water stewardship, and annual compliance reports.

changes.old: Regulates "large-load data centers" above 30 MW individual peak load or 60 MW collective load; includes renewable energy and hourly matching rules, water/electricity reporting, infrastructure cost contracts, model codes, site assessments, cumulative impact analysis, public engagement, community benefit agreements, and labor standards.
changes.new: Would regulate large-load data centers above 30 MW individual peak load or 60 MW collective load, including specified expansions; would impose conditional utility interconnection and supply restrictions, renewable energy and hourly matching rules, water and electricity reporting, infrastructure cost contracts, model codes, site assessments, cumulative impact analysis, public engagement, community benefit agreements, and labor standards.
